=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text minus "-"
text data "5 0 1 2 2 3 5 1 1 0 5 6 9 8 0 1"
text twr "writes: "
global vals long 16
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note emiti writes a signed n; the magnitude is taken as a ulong so the minimum long cannot overflow
fn emiti n long to void
if lt n 0
emit minus
emitu add bitcast ulong not n 1
else
emitu ulong n
end
end
note parse reads the decimal numbers in s (separated by spaces, an optional - sign) into vals and
note returns how many; one pass over s, so the loop is bounded by len s
fn parse s view uchar * to ulong
n = ulong 0
v = long 0
sg = long 1
dig = false
for i ulong len s
c = get s i
if eq c 45
sg = long -1
else
if and ge c 48 le c 57
v = add mul v 10 long sub c 48
dig = true
else
if dig
put vals n mul sg v
n = add n 1
end
v = long 0
sg = long 1
dig = false
end
end
end
if dig
put vals n mul sg v
n = add n 1
end
ret n
end
note show writes vals[0..n-1] separated by spaces, then a newline
fn show n ulong to void
for i ulong n
if gt i 0
emit sp
end
emiti get vals i
end
emit nl
end
note place counts the elements after vals[c] that are smaller than item: that is item's sorted position
fn place c ulong n ulong item long to ulong
p = c
for x ulong sub sub n c 1
if lt get vals add add c x 1 item
p = add p 1
end
end
ret p
end
note cysort rotates each cycle into place, writing every misplaced element exactly once, and returns
note the number of writes; each rotation pass writes one element, so n passes bound one cycle
fn cysort n ulong to ulong
w = ulong 0
for c ulong sub n 1
item = get vals c
p = place c n item
if eq p c
continue
end
while eq item get vals p bound 16
p = add p 1
end
t = get vals p
put vals p item
item = t
w = add w 1
while ne p c bound 16
p = place c n item
while eq item get vals p bound 16
p = add p 1
end
t = get vals p
put vals p item
item = t
w = add w 1
end
end
ret w
end
fn main to int
n = parse data
show n
w = cysort n
show n
emit twr
emitu w
emit nl
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}
<pre>
5 0 1 2 2 3 5 1 1 0 5 6 9 8 0 1
0 0 0 1 1 1 1 2 2 3 5 5 5 6 8 9
writes: 14
</pre>
